message.content:
Below is a step‑by‑step guide – plus ready‑to‑copy examples – for building a **RESTful GET** request against the *Cisco Nexus Dashboard* (ND) v6.3.1 to fetch “speed” data for a specific interface.

---

## 1️⃣ What you’ll need

| Item | Why it matters |
|------|----------------|
| **Dashboard host/IP** | `192.120.45.67` |
| **Endpoint** | `/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo` |
| **HTTP verb** | `GET` |
| **Query params** | `fabricName`, `nodeId`, `podId`, `interfaceType`, `infoType` |
| **Auth** | ND supports either **Basic Auth** (`username/password`) or **Bearer Token** obtained through the OAuth2 flow. |

> ⚠️ If your dashboard has a self‑signed certificate, add `--insecure/-k` to skip TLS validation when testing locally.

---

## 2️⃣ Build the raw URI

```text
https://<dashboard-ip>/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo?<query>
```

Plugging in your values gives:

```text
https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo?
   fabricName=Network1&
   nodeId=12&
   podId=10&
   interfaceType=Ethernet&
   infoType=Speed
```

(Spaces removed → one continuous line.)

---

## 3️⃣ Authentication options  

### A. Basic Auth (quick test)

If you have a local account on ND:

```bash
curl --insecure \
     -u admin:admin123 \          # <-- replace with real creds
     "https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo?\
      fabricName=Network1&nodeId=12&podId=10&interfaceType=Ethernet&infoType=Speed"
```

Result will look something like:

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "interface": "Eth0/24",
      "speedMbps": 10000,
      ...
    }
  ]
}
```

### B. Bearer Token (recommended for production)

#### Step 1 – Get a token  
Use the ND OAuth2 endpoint (replace `<client_id>` & `<secret>`):

```bash
TOKEN_RESPONSE=$(curl --silent --request POST \
  --header "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  --data-urlencode "grant_type=password" \
  --data-urlencode "username=<your_user>" \
  --data-urlencode "password=<your_pass>" \
  --data-urlencode "scope=read" \
  "https://192.120.45.67/oauth/token")

export ACCESS_TOKEN=$(echo "$TOKEN_RESPONSE" | jq -r .access_token)
```

*(Make sure `jq` is installed.)*

#### Step 2 – Call the API with the token

```bash
curl --insecure \
     -H "Accept: application/json" \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
     "https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo?\
      fabricName=Network1&nodeId=12&podId=10&interfaceType=Ethernet&infoType=Speed"
```

---

## 4️⃣ Full Python Example (requests lib)

```python
import os
import json
import requests

BASE_URL = "https://192.120.45.67"

def get_access_token(username, password):
    url = f"{BASE_URL}/oauth/token"
    payload = {
        "grant_type": "password",
        "username": username,
        "password": password,
        "scope": "read"
    }
    r = requests.post(url, data=payload, verify=False)  # verify=False skips cert check
    return r.json()["access_token"]

def get_speed(fabric_name, node_id, pod_id, iface_type="Ethernet", info_type="Speed"):
    token = get_access_token("admin", "admin123")  # change creds
    api_url = (
        f"{BASE_URL}/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo?"
        f"fabricName={fabric_name}&nodeId={node_id}"
        f"&podId={pod_id}&interfaceType={iface_type}&infoType={info_type}"
    )
    headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}", "Accept": "application/json"}
    resp = requests.get(api_url, headers=headers, verify=False)
    print(json.dumps(resp.json(), indent=2))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    get_speed("Network1", 12, 10)
```

> 👉 Replace `"admin"` / `"admin123"` with actual ND credentials.  
> 👉 Set `verify=True` once you install a trusted CA bundle.

---

## 5️⃣ Quick Checklist before running

| ✅ | Checkpoint |
|----|------------|
| ✔︎ Verify DNS/IP resolves correctly. |
| ✔︎ Confirm port 443 (HTTPS) open between client & ND. |
| ✔︎ Ensure your user has at least **Read** rights on the target fabric/node. |
| ✔︎ For production, enable proper TLS certificates instead of `--insecure`. |
| ✔︎ Inspect returned JSON schema—fields may vary slightly across firmware releases. |

---

## 🎉 Done!

With those snippets you can hit the ND API directly from CLI, scripts, or even Postman. Happy querying!
